notes_for_us: Nothing in the fifteen genres describes a vehicle journey. Racing's own boundary note says no lap and no finish means Simulation, but this has a finish and no competition; Simulation is a job loop; Survival is threat evasion in a bounded space; Adventure is a journey on foot. I got a workable build by leading Survival and borrowing Adventure's corridor, and the road still ended up as a walking trail.

The prompt's whole hook is that the world changes every run - a lake replaces the road, an avalanche reroutes it, a village appears sometimes. The handoff can only describe one fixed arrangement. There is no way to mark a piece of geometry as conditional, alternate, or present-on-some-runs, so the single most important thing this user said about their map cannot be written down.

notes_for_us: The scale band system assumes a humanoid player. Every row of the table is written in human units - furniture, street lights, city blocks - and the cross-check is the 16-studs-per-second avatar. For a player who is an ant, 'furniture' and 'coastline' are the same question asked at two different magnifications, and I could not answer the band honestly. The handoff has no field saying how big the player is, which for this prompt is the single most load-bearing fact in it.

Nothing in either skill says what language to emit in. The user wrote Spanish; the option text is a template in English and the free text is the place their own words would go. I wrote English throughout on the assumption the image model reads it, but that is a guess and 'keep the user's own words' points the other way.

notes_for_us: The only shape that can express 'goes on forever indoors' is interior-endless, and it is filed under Survival, whose whole option set assumes something is chasing you. A user who explicitly removed the monster still has to be classified as horror survival to reach the right shape, and then two thirds of the preset has to be parked. Shapes being shared solved half of this; presets are still welded to their genre's threat model.

Also: 'no entities' is a prohibition, and constraints/build_rule held it well - but nothing checks it. spawner-npc sits in the emitted handoff next to a constraint forbidding it, and only the notes say which one wins.
